newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Executives arrested as bank woes loom in Vietnam.
newsitem.headline: Executives arrested as bank woes loom in Vietnam.

text.p: Vietnam reported on Tuesday the arrest of two prominent business executives amid concerns over serious loans problems in the national banking system arising from failed property speculation.

Company officials and state investigators said Tang Minh Phung of the Ho Chi Minh City firm Minh Phung had been detained by police on Monday on a charge of "taking advantage of confidence to appropriate citizens' and socialist property".
Tuesday's state-controlled media reported that a second senior executive, Lien Khui Thin of trading firm EPCO, had also been arrested on the same charge.

Minh Phung, a major garment-exporter with interests in several other sectors, is among several companies under scrutiny recently for their involvement in Vietnam's brief property market boom of the early 1990s.

In a series of interviews last week, senior Vietnamese economists and bankers told Reuters that borrowing by some local firms to fund real estate speculation had left the domestic banking system owing millions of dollars from debt gone bad.
A senior official at the State Bank of Vietnam, the central bank, identified Minh Phung as one of the firms involved.

"It's a serious problem," said Tran Trong Do, banking operations director at the State Bank. "Due to our poor experience in supervision, big problems have been caused for the national banking system."

Economists said the firms involved had used influence and connections to secure huge multiple loans from both private joint-stock and state owned commercial banks, usually in the form of letters of credit.

A downturn in the property market since 1995 had left these firms unable to repay debts to banks, which in turn were having to delay repayments on letters of credit because collateral on loans had been taken in the form of difficult-to-recover fixed real-estate assets.
Official figures were not available, but rough estimates by bankers put overall debt levels at around $1 billion with total overdue payments at around $500 million.
Tuesday's state-controlled media said the charges against the directors of Minh Phung and EPCO were under articles of Vietnam's criminal code. The possible penalties were not specified.
Correspondents in Ho Chi Minh City said business appeared to be continuing as normal at EPCO on Tuesday. Minh Phung's head office was closed but phone queries were answered.

Indications of the problems first surfaced in February when the Joint-Stock Commercial Bank for Private Enterprise (VP Bank) came under scrutiny for extending the payment period under a letter of credit to South Korea's Ssangyong.
State Bank officials told Reuters the authorities were seriously concerned about the extent of the problem and said measures to tackle it were being worked out.
